biography: Mario Josten, born in the shadow of the Nürburgring, practically inhaled gasoline fumes from birth. His father, a mechanic for a local touring car team, instilled in him a love for speed and precision. Mario's early racing career was a whirlwind of karting triumphs and near misses in Formula Ford, marked by flashes of brilliance overshadowed by unpredictable outbursts. A defining moment came at the VLN Endurance Championship, where, filling in for an injured driver, he wrestled a heavily damaged BMW M3 E46 GTR to a podium finish, earning him a contract with the team. Now at 28, Josten is considered a driver brimming with raw talent, but struggling to maintain the consistency needed to truly contend for championships.
drivingStyle: Josten's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos'. He possesses an uncanny ability to find grip where others don't dare, often throwing the car into corners with a late-braking, aggressive style. While breathtaking to watch, this approach often leads to tire degradation and inconsistency throughout a race distance. He's known for his lightning-fast reflexes and his ability to improvise in changing conditions, but also for his occasional over-eagerness, resulting in costly mistakes.

rivalries.reason: A fellow German touring car driver known for his calculated and methodical approach, Richter represents everything Josten isn't, creating a clash of styles and personalities on and off the track.
A rising star in the GT ranks, Dubois has consistently outperformed Josten, fueling his competitive fire and leading to several on-track altercations.
Bellini and Josten have a history of close calls and accusations of overly aggressive maneuvers, stemming from a controversial incident at the 24 Hours of Spa.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to classical music precisely 30 minutes before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to eat anything yellow on race day.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being perfect, it's about being fearless. If you're not on the edge, you're wasting time."
careerHighlight: His improbable podium finish at the VLN Endurance Championship, driving a damaged car for over two hours and battling against seasoned veterans, securing his professional contract.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the ADAC GT Masters race at the Sachsenring due to an overly aggressive overtaking attempt.
